small_guidance:
- The conv3d (torch cuDNN) now dominates runtime; tuning the post-conv fusion further has minimal headroom. Within the current fused kernel, try BLOCK_S=512/1024 with num_warps=8 and num_stages=3, and consider merging the stats pass into a single persistent kernel per (N,C) row that keeps x resident in registers/SMEM and writes mean/invstd to shared, avoiding the second global read.
- Replace the two-kernel stats+apply path with a single persistent kernel per (N,) that loops C×S, computing per-channel mean/invstd online (Welford or sum/sumsq) in registers, then immediately doing clamp+mul+max reduction across C — eliminates the intermediate mean/invstd global tensors.
- Use channels-last (N, S, C) layout for the post-conv tensor so the C-reduction (max over channels) is contiguous; a transpose may pay for itself given C=16 is tiny.
large_guidance:
- The conv3d is now the bottleneck (fast_p ≈ 0.95, post-conv already fused). Replace nn.Conv3d with a custom Triton im2col-style GEMM kernel: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), with implicit im2col gather. Shapes are tiny (OC=16, kernel=3³=27, IC=3 → K=81), so use BLOCK_M=16 (OC), BLOCK_N=128 (spatial), BLOCK_K=81 fully unrolled, and fold the conv bias into the epilogue.
- Fuse the entire pipeline end-to-end: conv epilogue computes y = (conv_out + bias) * multiplier_c, accumulates per-channel sum/sumsq into shared, then a second pass (or persistent within the same program if the (N, spatial) tile fits) applies normalization, clamp, multiplier, and channel-max — writing only the final [N, D, H, W] output. This eliminates the materialized [N,16,14,30,30] conv output tensor.
- If full fusion is too complex, at minimum write the custom conv3d kernel with bias+multiplier folded into its epilogue and write the result in (N, S, C) channels-last layout to feed a fast channel-reduction post-kernel.
